key_insight: SurgRec provides a scalable, reproducible pretraining recipe and large multi-source surgical video corpus (10,535 videos, 214.5M frames) that enables stronger, generalizable video representations via two instantiations: SurgRec‑MAE and SurgRec‑JEPA.
problem_solved: Addresses limited data scale, narrow procedural diversity, and inconsistent/reproducible training pipelines in surgical foundation models, which have hindered robust video representation learning and fair benchmark comparisons.
method: Curate a large multi-source surgical video corpus (10,535 videos, ~214.5M frames) to increase scale and procedural diversity.
Design a reproducible pretraining recipe (SurgRec) instantiated as two self-supervised variants: SurgRec‑MAE (masked autoencoding) and SurgRec‑JEPA (joint-embedding predictive architecture).
Provide standardized training protocols and evaluation to enable consistent benchmarking and transfer to downstream surgical tasks.
impact: Makes surgical video pretraining practical and comparable: practitioners gain a reproducible recipe and large-scale pretrained models that improve transfer performance across surgical tasks, reduce reliance on manual annotation, and accelerate clinical AI development.
visual_elements: Dataset infographic: stacked bars or icons showing 10,535 videos and 214.5M frames with procedural diversity breakdown.
Pipeline diagram: end-to-end flow from multi-source video curation → SurgRec pretraining → downstream tasks/benchmarks.
Architecture comparison: side‑by‑side boxes for SurgRec‑MAE vs SurgRec‑JEPA highlighting key differences (e.g., masked reconstruction vs predictive embedding).
Benchmark chart: bar chart showing improved downstream task metrics (e.g., segmentation/classification) vs prior baselines.
paper_title: Scaling Video Pretraining for Surgical Foundation Models
paper_authors: Sicheng Lu, Zikai Xiao, Jianhui Wei, Danyu Sun, Qi Lu
